newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 7.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Friday.

- Former Fine Gael minister Michael Lowry resigned from the party on Thursday night after failing to meet an end-of-February deadline to get his tax affairs in order set by Irish Prime Minister John Bruton.
- The man Irish police suspect of killing crime journalist Vernoica Guerin said on Thursday: "I didn't kill her and I don't know who did."

- The booming economy is reflected in the latest figures for advertising revenue in national newspapers. Last year space bought by advertisers reached a record 108.5 million punts, up 18 per cent for the corresponding period in 1995.

- Former Fine Gael minister Michael Lowry is likely to run as an independent candidate in the forthcoming general election following the decision by Irish Prime Minister John Bruton that he would not allow Lowry run for Fine Gael.

- Fianna Fail, the main opposition party, has promised to build 2,000 prison spaces and recruit 1,200 more Irish police if elected to government but admitted that it had not worked out what the measures would cost.

- Irish police have warned that the suspects in the murder of crime journalist Veronica Guerin murder inquiry have embarked on a self-publicity campaign so that they can later claim that their chances of getting a fair trial have been prejudiced.
- Ireland's Minister for Finance, Ruairi Quinn, has expressed serious concern that increasing house prices could feed through to higher inflation.
- Irish economists are still divided on the benefits of EMU for Ireland, particularly if Britain stays out of the single currency.
- The man Irish police believe fired the gun that assassinated crime journalist Veronica Guerin insisted on Thursday night: "I did not kill her."
- Irish police have smashed a nation-wide car smuggling ring involving vehicles stolen in the UK.
